QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_39

question.text: Data quality indicators listed in Section 5.11.4 include Validity, Reliability, Completeness, Integrity, and Timelines. Which pairing is CORRECT?

answer.text: Reliability — data is up to date and prompt
Validity — whether data collected measures what it is intended to measure
Integrity — whether data measurements are based on standard methodologies
Timelines — data is protected from bias or manipulation

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 5.11.4 defines: Validity — whether data measures what it is intended to measure. Reliability — based on standard methodologies. Completeness — all aspects captured. Integrity — protected from bias or manipulation. Timelines — data is up to date and prompt. Only Option B matches correctly. **The Trap:** A swaps Reliability with Timelines. C swaps Integrity with Reliability. D swaps Timelines with Integrity. Systematic pair-swap distractor. **Cross-Exam Context:** These dimensions are standard in data-quality literature used across NISM exams — XXIII uniquely applies them to beneficiary survey data. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Stamp every raw data file with a header noting source, date, and collection method — this single practice resolves Validity, Reliability, and Timelines questions in one working-paper artefact.
